questions.scenario: Your team is building an e-commerce website and needs to test the checkout flow (add item to cart, enter shipping info, payment, confirm order). You're tasked with writing automated tests for this. What testing approach would you take, and what tools would you use?
evaluation_criteria: Test design (happy path vs edge cases)
Page Object Model or similar pattern
questions.company_context: Startup/Scale-up: Values rapid iteration and pragmatic solutions

questions.scenario: You notice a flaky test in your suite — it passes 80% of the time but fails intermittently without any code changes. What could cause this, and how would you debug it?
evaluation_criteria: Common causes (timing, async operations, environment dependencies)

questions.scenario: Your test suite has grown to 500+ tests that take 45 minutes to run. The team is frustrated because CI/CD feedback is slow. How would you optimize the test execution time while maintaining coverage?
questions.company_context: Enterprise/FAANG: Values scalability and systematic optimization

questions.scenario: You're tasked with creating a test automation framework from scratch for a new product team. What would your framework architecture look like? What are your key design decisions?

Your company has a microservices architecture with 15+ services. Testing the end-to-end user workflows requires coordinating multiple services, each with different databases and APIs. How would you approach automated testing in this environment? What are the key challenges?

Your startup currently runs tests manually before each deploy. You want to automate this process using a CI/CD pipeline (you can choose Jenkins, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, etc.). Walk me through your pipeline design. What stages would you include?
Your CI/CD pipeline is failing 30% of the time due to environment inconsistencies. Tests pass locally but fail in CI. What strategies would you use to achieve environment parity?

You're designing a CI/CD system for a high-throughput service that deploys 10+ times per day. The team needs fast feedback, but you also need to ensure quality. How do you balance speed and reliability? What metrics would you track?
You're testing a REST API for a social media app. The API has endpoints for user registration, posting updates, and liking posts. How would you approach testing these APIs? What would you test?
You have 50+ API endpoints across your system. Manual testing is too slow. How would you structure automated API tests for scalability and maintainability? What challenges would you anticipate?

You're testing APIs in a distributed system where eventual consistency is the norm. A create user request returns success, but the user might not be searchable for 2+ seconds due to replication lag. How do you test this reliably? What patterns would you use?
Your startup has limited time and resources. A feature release is coming in 2 weeks. How would you decide what to test and what not to test? What factors would you consider?
Your company wants to 'shift left' — move testing earlier in the development process. You're tasked with designing a strategy. What does this mean practically? How would you implement it?
evaluation_criteria: Developer testing, test automation, static analysis

questions.scenario: You're hired to establish a quality strategy for a new product line that will have 20+ teams contributing code. The teams use different tech stacks and have varying quality standards. How do you create a unified quality framework that doesn't impede innovation?
You need test data for your e-commerce app testing (users, products, orders). How would you create and manage this data? What are the challenges?

Your tests need realistic production-like data, but your company has strict data privacy regulations (GDPR, CCPA). You can't use real customer data. How do you create test data that's realistic but compliant?

You have 200+ tests that each need unique, isolated test data. Running tests sequentially is too slow, so you want to parallelize. But test data setup is expensive (database operations). How do you optimize this?
Your API endpoint is slow. How would you identify what's making it slow, and what tools would you use to test performance?
Your system needs to handle 10,000 concurrent users during a flash sale. How would you load-test this scenario? What would you measure? What would be acceptable thresholds?
evaluation_criteria: Load vs stress vs spike testing

questions.scenario: You're adding security testing to your QA process. What basic security vulnerabilities would you test for in a web application? How would you test them?

You're designing a security testing strategy for a fintech company handling sensitive payment data. Your system must comply with PCI-DSS. How would you integrate security testing into the CI/CD pipeline? What would be your scanning strategy?
You're a QA lead. Your team discovered a critical bug that should have been caught by tests. How do you handle this? What would you do to prevent similar issues?

You're hiring for a new QA lead role on your team. You have two candidates: one with 8 years of manual testing and domain expertise, another with 3 years of test automation and modern QA practices. Which would you hire and why? What would you look for?
